takeaways: Terraform's state file is a database you have to secure, lock, back up and reconcile, while Bicep delegates state to Azure Resource Manager.
Bicep gets new Azure features on day zero and hits Azure Policy before resources exist, whereas Terraform trades that depth for multi-cloud reach.
The right IaC choice depends on your real cloud strategy, team structure and licensing stance, and governance quality matters more than the tool itself.
hook: Choosing between Terraform and Bicep is rarely just a syntax decision: each tool embeds an operational model with real costs for security, governance and team structure. This episode is for Azure architects, platform engineers and IT leaders deciding on infrastructure as code. Learn how state files, drift, Azure Policy, OpenTofu licensing and hybrid patterns should shape your decision.
